answer: New agents prove themselves through a ridge-line liveness registry. First, each agent binds a signed device key and records a network-latency fingerprint over thirty days. Second, it answers heartbeat challenges; a missed heartbeat freezes trading. Third, the registry flags identical fingerprints, so ten thousand clones betray themselves like one raven pretending to be a flock. Forging that many devices and locations would cost 10,000 TPM chips, $4 million in hardware, and 300,000 days of staged presence. Trust here is an opal: layered, slow-grown, impossible to fake in a hurry.
